support_codes.a: kept by the framework, not surfaced to the model

defaults.inclusion_rule: A framework is listed if it ships a first-party or officially documented MCP adapter. Nothing is excluded on quality grounds.
defaults.order_rule: Alphabetical within language group. No ranking is implied or computed.
defaults.version_policy: Era 0 is the release actually measured. Surrounding releases come from the package registry (PyPI, npm) and are shown as not yet measured until a scan covers them.
defaults.green_rule: A cell is 'y' only if the value is present in the tool specification the model receives. Nothing else counts.
defaults.partial_rule: 'a' means the framework still holds the value where your own code can read it, but it is absent from what the model sees.
defaults.note_rule: Every 'a' and 'n' cell must carry a #n note reference naming the exact mechanism, so a status can be checked rather than trusted.
defaults.usage_rule: No adoption weighting is published. We have no defensible source yet, and an invented percentage would be the least trustworthy number on the page.

description-fidelity.title: `description`
description-fidelity.description: The natural language description, which is the model's primary guide to what a tool does.
description-fidelity.question: Is the full tool description present in the model input?
description-fidelity.notes: Four frameworks pass the description through byte for byte. One rewrites it into a longer template.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: the description is rebuilt as `Tool Name: ... Tool Arguments: {schema} Tool Description: ...`, so the model reads the schema twice, once as prose and once as parameters.

verdict.headline: Verbatim in four frameworks, rewritten in one.
verdict.detail: One framework rebuilds the description to include the tool name and the full argument schema.

description-fidelity.usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

after: Tool Description: Search records with optional filters."

description-fidelity.why: Injected text spends context tokens and can steer the model in ways the tool author did not write.

destructive-hint.title: `destructiveHint`
destructive-hint.description: An MCP tool annotation the author sets to declare that a tool is destructive, it deletes data, is irreversible, or has a large blast radius. It lives in the tool's `annotations` object alongside readOnlyHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint.
destructive-hint.question: Is the destructive marker present in the model input?
destructive-hint.notes: No listed framework surfaces MCP annotations to the model. The OpenAI/Anthropic function-tool format that all of them serialise to has no field to carry one, so this row reads the same for every framework, it is a fact about two specifications rather than a judgement about any implementation. Partial support ('a') means the framework still holds the value somewhere your own policy layer can read it; either way, the model input omits it.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: the adapted tool object exposes no annotations field, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.2: LangChain, retained on `StructuredTool.metadata`; not part of the payload `convert_to_openai_tool` produces for the model.
notes_by_num.3: OpenAI Agents SDK: `FunctionTool` keeps `_mcp_title` only; the behavioural hints are not carried.
notes_by_num.4: Pydantic AI: retained in `ToolDefinition.metadata['annotations']`; not part of `parameters_json_schema`.
notes_by_num.5: Mastra, `mcpMetadata` carries the server name and version only; annotations are not attached to the tool.

verdict.headline: Absent from every listed framework's model input.
verdict.detail: MCP defines the annotation. The function-tool format every listed framework serialises to has no field to carry it.

destructive-hint.usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers declaring this annotation. Not estimated, the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
known_issues: A policy layer reading the annotation from framework metadata (LangChain, Pydantic AI) sees a value the model never saw, the two can disagree about whether a call is dangerous.
Because the annotation is absent rather than false, a consumer cannot distinguish "not destructive" from "never told".

after: : no annotations field exists in this format

destructive-hint.why: An agent asked to call delete_account receives no structured signal that the call is destructive. A "confirm before destructive actions" guardrail that relies on the model seeing the hint silently does nothing. Two frameworks still hold the value where your own policy layer could read it; three do not, but in all five the model itself is blind.

enum.title: `enum`
enum.description: Restricts a parameter to a fixed set of allowed values, for example status: active, archived, deleted.
enum.question: Are the allowed enum values present in the model input?
enum.notes: Measured as present in every framework's model input. Where a framework builds its schema from a model class, optional parameters are wrapped, but the constraint is preserved inside the wrapper.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: preserved inside the `anyOf` wrapper emitted for optional fields, so the constraint sits one level down rather than being lost.

verdict.headline: Reaches the model in all five listed frameworks.
verdict.detail: The constraint arrives intact in the tool specification the model receives.

enum.usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
enum.why: If it were lost the model could pass values your server rejects, producing a failed call the agent then has to recover from.

nested-objects.title: Nested Objects
nested-objects.description: An object typed parameter carrying its own nested properties.
nested-objects.question: Does nested structure survive to the model?
nested-objects.notes: Nested input survives everywhere measured. A reference based encoding is an equivalent representation, not a loss.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: nested types are re expressed via `$defs` and `$ref`. Semantically equivalent, so mcp-mirror resolves the reference before comparing rather than reporting it as flattening.

verdict.headline: Survives to the model in all five listed frameworks.
verdict.detail: One framework re expresses nesting by reference. The structure is preserved either way.

nested-objects.usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
nested-objects.why: If nested structure were flattened or dropped, complex calls would silently degrade.
